newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank watchdog urges aid to Kia contractors.
newsitem.headline: Bank watchdog urges aid to Kia contractors.

text.p: The head of South Korea's Office of Bank Supervision urged "aggressive" financial aid on Monday to subcontractors of the troubled Kia Group.
In a meeting with presidents of 12 creditor banks, Rhee Soo-hyoo, bank superintendent, said credit lines to those companies should be maintained.
"By aggressively supporting funds to subcontractors of Kia Group, we can prevent a chain of possible defaults," Lee said.
About 5,000 companies are supplying parts and materials to the nation's eighth largest conglomerate.
Lee said financial institutions should continue to discount commercial papers issued by Kia Group, which would keep credit flowing into those companies.
In order to ease tight liquidity in creditor banks, Lee said the Bank of Korea would re-deem monetary stabilisation bonds bought by those banks before their maturity.
Lee said the central bank also extended the guarantee limit for Kia commercial papers.

Under the expanded limit, South Korea's credit guarantee institutions would be able to guarantee more Kia commercial papers, which would allow Kia subcontractors to raise money by discounting Kia commercial papers.

The total limit for guarantee institutions was raised to one trillion from the previous 500 billion won. The individual limit for a company seeking a guarantee normally is 100 million won, but the central bank raised the limit for Kia subcontractors to 200 million.
"If even one or two auto parts will not be supplied, assembly lines in Kia Group will stop. And its efforts to get business back to normal will be useless," said a central bank official.
An anticipated announcement by creditor banks on the rescue of the Kia Group did not materialise.
"Creditor banks will discuss the bail-out plan on July 30 as scheduled," said an official at Korea First Bank, Kia's major creditor.
Creditor banks decided to bail out 18 Kia Group affiliates last week to protect the group from imminent failure. The group's financial crisis has rocked the local financial industry.
